featuredRationale: Seed release with an official launch announcement and current model documentation.
summary: A non-reasoning API model for instruction following, tool calling, and broad-domain work.
intendedUse: Complex API tasks that benefit from the most capable model in the GPT-4.1 family.

featuredRationale: Seed release with an official launch announcement and current model documentation.
summary: A smaller, faster GPT-4.1 variant for instruction following and tool calling.
intendedUse: API tasks that prioritize lower latency while retaining instruction following and tool calling.

featuredRationale: Seed release with an official launch announcement and current model documentation.
summary: The fastest, most cost-efficient GPT-4.1 variant for instruction following and tool calling.
intendedUse: Classification, autocompletion, and API tasks that prioritize speed and cost efficiency.

featuredRationale: OpenAI's current flagship model, launched for general availability with an official announcement and dated API model documentation.
summary: The flagship tier of the GPT-5.6 family and OpenAI's most capable model for complex professional, coding, and agentic work. Its API documentation lists a 1,050,000-token context window and a 2026-02-16 knowledge cutoff, and the gpt-5.6 alias routes to Sol.
intendedUse: Complex professional, coding, and agentic tasks that call for OpenAI's highest-capability model.

featuredRationale: Launched in the GPT-5.6 general-availability announcement with its own dated API model documentation.
summary: The balanced cost-and-performance tier of the GPT-5.6 family, which OpenAI positions as competitive with GPT-5.5 at a lower cost. Its API documentation lists a 1,050,000-token context window and a 2026-02-16 knowledge cutoff, and says it roughly corresponds to the mini tier of earlier GPT-5 families.
intendedUse: Everyday professional and coding workloads that balance capability against cost.

featuredRationale: Launched in the GPT-5.6 general-availability announcement with its own dated API model documentation.
summary: The most affordable, highest-throughput tier of the GPT-5.6 family. Its API documentation lists a 1,050,000-token context window and a 2026-02-16 knowledge cutoff, and says it roughly corresponds to the nano tier of earlier GPT-5 families.
intendedUse: Cost-sensitive, high-volume workloads that still need GPT-5.6-generation capability.

summary: The GPT-5 generation before GPT-5.6, introduced in the API on 2026-04-23 for complex coding, research, and data-analysis work. Its API documentation lists a 1,050,000-token context window, a 2026-04-23 default snapshot, and a 2025-12-01 knowledge cutoff.
intendedUse: Complex coding, research, and professional workflows on the generation directly preceding GPT-5.6.

summary: An earlier GPT-5 generation, introduced on 2026-03-05 as OpenAI's frontier model for professional work, with state-of-the-art coding, computer use, and a roughly one-million-token context. Its API documentation lists a 1,050,000-token context window, a 2026-03-05 default snapshot, and a 2025-08-31 knowledge cutoff.
intendedUse: Professional coding and agentic work on the generation two steps before GPT-5.6.

summary: The first GPT-5 generation and the root of the line that GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.6 extend. Its release date is taken from the pinned API snapshot gpt-5-2025-08-07; OpenAI's documentation now labels GPT-5 a previous model and points users to GPT-5.6. The model documentation lists a 400,000-token context window and a 2024-09-30 knowledge cutoff.
intendedUse: Earlier-generation coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks; superseded by later GPT-5 generations.

featuredRationale: Anthropic's most capable widely released model, with a dated general-availability statement in the official model documentation.
summary: Anthropic's most capable widely released model, with adaptive thinking always on.
intendedUse: Long-running agent work that needs the highest available Claude capability.

summary: Shares Claude Fable 5's capabilities and specifications, but without the safety classifiers that can decline a request. Offered only in limited availability.
intendedUse: Defensive cybersecurity workflows for customers approved through Anthropic's Project Glasswing.

featuredRationale: The tier Anthropic recommends first for coding work that runs over many steps, with a dated launch announcement.
summary: A hosted Claude model for complex agent-driven coding and enterprise work.
intendedUse: Complex, multi-step coding and enterprise workloads.

featuredRationale: The only Claude 4.5 model still documented among current models, with a dated launch announcement.
summary: The fastest Claude model, and the only current one that still takes an explicit flag to turn extended thinking on or off.
intendedUse: Latency-sensitive work that still needs strong reasoning.

featuredRationale: The current Pro tier of the Gemini 3 generation, with a dated release record and a published model page.
summary: Refines the Gemini 3 Pro series with better thinking, improved token efficiency, and more grounded, factually consistent output.
intendedUse: Software engineering and multi-step automated workflows that need precise tool use.

featuredRationale: Generally available with a dated release, a scheduled shutdown, and a named replacement, which makes its lineage documented rather than inferred.
summary: A fast, lightweight model that accepts text, images, audio, and video, built for high-frequency, simple tasks.
intendedUse: High-volume automated workflows and simple data extraction where response speed is the main constraint.

featuredRationale: The named replacement for Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, with a dated release and published limits.
summary: A fast, lightweight model that accepts text, images, audio, and video, built for high-throughput work and document parsing.
intendedUse: High-volume automated workflows, simple data extraction, and document understanding.

featuredRationale: Historically important: the generally available Pro tier of the generation that preceded Gemini 3, still documented with no announced shutdown on the Gemini API.
summary: Google's most advanced Gemini 2.5 reasoning model, able to work across text, audio, images, video, and entire code repositories.
intendedUse: Complex reasoning over large datasets, codebases, and documents.

featuredRationale: Historically important: a reasoning-capable Flash model released to general availability alongside Gemini 2.5 Pro.
summary: The balanced tier of Gemini 2.5, able to reason step by step before answering.
intendedUse: Large-scale, low-latency, high-volume tasks that still require thinking.

featuredRationale: Meta's current downloadable multimodal model, with a dated model card and a licence that states its own effective date.
summary: Accepts text and images together, and can read up to 10 million tokens in one request — a token is one of the small chunks that text and images are broken into. It is divided into 16 specialist sections, and each token is handled by only a fraction of the model: 17 billion of its 109 billion parameters.
intendedUse: Assistant-style chat and visual reasoning across the twelve languages the model card lists.

featuredRationale: Announced in the same launch as Llama 4 Scout, with its own model card and published weight formats.
summary: Accepts text and images together. It is divided into 128 specialist sections plus one shared section, and each token — one of the small chunks that text and images are broken into — goes to the shared section and a single specialist, using 17 billion of its 400 billion parameters. Weights are published at two levels of numeric precision, BF16 and the smaller FP8.
intendedUse: Assistant-style chat, visual reasoning, and code generation.

featuredRationale: Historically important: the largest Llama 3.1 size, with a release date stated in both the model card and the licence.
summary: The largest Llama 3.1 size. Text only, and it reads up to 128,000 tokens at once — a token is one of the small chunks that text is broken into.
intendedUse: Multilingual dialogue and natural language generation across the eight languages the model card lists.

featuredRationale: The model card and licence agree on its release date.
summary: A text-only 70-billion-parameter model tuned to follow instructions rather than simply continue text, which Meta optimised for multilingual dialogue.
intendedUse: Assistant-style multilingual chat.

summary: A purpose-trained cybersecurity model in the GPT-5.6 family, offered as the gpt-5.6-cyber alias for approved defenders conducting authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation, and security testing. Access requires separate approval through OpenAI's Daybreak program and is served via the Daybreak Red channel. Its API documentation lists text and image input, text output, a 400,000-token context window, 128,000 max output tokens, and a 2026-02-16 knowledge cutoff, and it is offered on the Responses endpoint (Chat Completions is not supported). Its release date is taken from the 2026-08-10 announcement because the model documentation page carries no date.
intendedUse: Authorized, governed cybersecurity work - vulnerability research, exploit validation, and security testing - by defenders approved for OpenAI's Daybreak program.

summary: The single release of the GPT-5.1 generation. Its release date is taken from the pinned API snapshot gpt-5.1-2025-11-13, the same way the GPT-5 record is dated, because the model documentation page carries no launch date. That page lists a 400,000-token context window, 128,000 max output tokens, text and image input, text output, and a 2024-09-30 knowledge cutoff. The page still describes GPT-5.1 as OpenAI's flagship model while the model catalogue names GPT-5.6 Sol as the flagship; that disagreement is recorded as an unresolved conflict rather than smoothed over.
intendedUse: Coding and agentic tasks with configurable reasoning and non-reasoning effort, on a generation OpenAI no longer lists in its current model catalogue.

summary: The single release of the GPT-5.2 generation, which OpenAI's model documentation calls its previous frontier model for complex professional work and points to GPT-5.6 instead. Its release date is taken from the pinned API snapshot gpt-5.2-2025-12-11. The documentation lists a 400,000-token context window, 128,000 max output tokens, text and image input, text output, and a 2025-08-31 knowledge cutoff.
intendedUse: Complex professional work with configurable reasoning effort, on a generation OpenAI documents as superseded by GPT-5.6.

summary: A Codex-native model optimized for agentic coding tasks in Codex or similar environments. Its release date is taken from the OpenAI news item 'Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex', which carries pubDate 5 February 2026, because the model documentation page lists only the dateless gpt-5.3-codex identifier and no dated snapshot. The documentation lists a 400,000-token context window, 128,000 max output tokens, text and image input, text output, and a 2025-08-31 knowledge cutoff.
intendedUse: Agentic coding tasks in Codex or similar environments, and long-horizon technical work.

summary: OpenAI's image generation and editing model, listed in the model catalogue as the current image model. Its release date is taken from the pinned API snapshot gpt-image-2-2026-04-21 because the model documentation page carries no launch date. The documentation lists text and image input and image output, and states no context window or maximum output, so neither is recorded.
intendedUse: Fast, high-quality image generation and editing, including edits from multiple high-fidelity image inputs.

featuredRationale: The current Sonnet-tier model in the Claude 5 lineup, with a dated general-availability launch and full specifications in Anthropic's model documentation.
summary: A hosted Claude model that Anthropic positions as the best combination of speed and intelligence, and describes as its most agentic Sonnet model to date.
intendedUse: Agentic work such as planning, tool use, coding, and knowledge work where speed and cost matter alongside capability.

featuredRationale: A generally available Flash tier of the Gemini 3 generation, with a dated release, an announced retirement window, and published token limits.
summary: A Gemini 3 Flash model offering sustained frontier-level intelligence at higher speed and lower cost, with near-Pro coding proficiency and parallel agentic execution.
intendedUse: Sub-agent deployment, multi-step workflows, and long-horizon agentic and coding tasks at scale.

featuredRationale: A generally available Flash tier of the Gemini 3 generation, with a dated release and published token limits.
summary: A Gemini 3 Flash model optimized for multi-step orchestration, full-stack code refactoring, and general reasoning, with improved token efficiency over Gemini 3.5 Flash.
intendedUse: Multi-step orchestration, code refactoring, and agentic execution across coding and multimodal tasks.

featuredRationale: The newest generally available Flash tier of the Gemini 3 generation, with a dated release and published token limits.
summary: The high-efficiency, cost-effective Flash model of the Gemini 3 family, delivering Pro-level agentic capabilities with strong code generation and terminal execution.
intendedUse: Primary agentic workhorse for high-throughput multimodal and coding workloads.

summary: Muse Spark is the first model in Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse family, described as a natively multimodal reasoning model with tool use, visual chain of thought, and multi-agent orchestration.
intendedUse: Multimodal reasoning with tool use and multi-agent orchestration.

featuredRationale: Meta Superintelligence Labs' latest Muse reasoning model, with a stated 1 million token context window and availability via the Meta Model API.
summary: Muse Spark 1.1 is Meta Superintelligence Labs' multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with a context window of 1 million tokens, offered to developers via the Meta Model API.
intendedUse: Agentic, tool-using multimodal reasoning over long-context inputs.

summary: Muse Image is Meta Superintelligence Labs' image generation model, available across the Meta AI app.
intendedUse: Text-to-image generation.

summary: Muse Video is a video generation model built on the same pretraining base as Muse Image, with native audio support, announced as coming soon to creators and Meta AI.
intendedUse: Text-to-video generation with native audio.

summary: Llama 3.2 1B is a text-only Llama 3.2 model for multilingual dialogue, agentic retrieval, summarization, and writing tasks, with a 128,000-token context length.
intendedUse: Assistant-style multilingual chat, agentic knowledge retrieval, summarization, mobile writing assistance, and query or prompt rewriting.

summary: Llama 3.2 3B is a text-only Llama 3.2 model for multilingual dialogue, agentic retrieval, summarization, and writing tasks, with a 128,000-token context length.
intendedUse: Assistant-style multilingual chat, agentic knowledge retrieval, summarization, mobile writing assistance, and query or prompt rewriting.

summary: Llama 3.2 11B Vision is a Llama 3.2 Vision model for image reasoning, visual recognition, captioning, and chat with images, with a 128,000-token context length.
intendedUse: Visual recognition, image reasoning, image captioning, assistant-style chat with images, and other image reasoning tasks.

summary: Llama 3.2 90B Vision is a Llama 3.2 Vision model for image reasoning, visual recognition, captioning, and chat with images, with a 128,000-token context length.
intendedUse: Visual recognition, image reasoning, image captioning, assistant-style chat with images, and other image reasoning tasks.

summary: Served only through the creator’s hosted API, with no downloadable weights and no licence offered for the weights, so no licence is recorded. Its documentation states a 500,000-token context window, text and image input with text output, and a knowledge cut-off of 1 February 2026. No parameter count is published anywhere the creator documents this model, so none is recorded here.
intendedUse: Coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work through the creator’s hosted API.

summary: Served only through the creator’s hosted API, with no downloadable weights and so no licence record. Its documentation states a 500,000-token context window and text and image input with text output, and publishes no parameter count. Three API names resolve to this one model: grok-4.5, grok-4.5-latest, and grok-build-latest. The last of those is an alias and not the separate grok-build-0.1 model listed on the same pricing page.
intendedUse: Agentic software, engineering, and workflow tasks through the creator’s hosted API.

summary: A sparse mixture-of-experts model available both through the creator’s hosted platform and as downloadable weights, under a licence the OSI approves. Those are recorded as two separate claims: the hosted API does not follow from the licence, and the licence does not follow from the weights being downloadable. The announcement states 675B total and 41B active parameters and is the figure recorded; the model card’s own architecture list says 673B with 39B active plus a 2.5B vision encoder, and that disagreement is left visible rather than reconciled.
intendedUse: General instruction following, multilingual conversation, and image understanding, either hosted or self-deployed.

summary: The middle size of the three Ministral 3 models announced together, published as downloadable weights under an OSI-approved licence with a 256k context window and a 0.4B vision encoder. The 3B and 14B sizes, and the base and reasoning variants of each size, are published in the same collection and are deliberately not enumerated here.
intendedUse: On-device and edge deployment where text and image understanding are needed without a hosted dependency.

summary: Weights are downloadable, and the licence is not one the OSI approves: the card calls it a "Modified MIT License" of the creator’s own drafting, so no SPDX identifier is recorded and the OSI claim is false while the downloadable claim is true. Released the same day as the 24B model, which carries Apache 2.0 instead, so one announcement covers two models under two different licences. Text is the only input recorded: this card lists no vision capability, while the 24B card published beside it does, so the difference is what each card states rather than an omission here.
intendedUse: Agentic software engineering: exploring codebases, editing multiple files, and driving software engineering agents.

summary: The smaller of the two Devstral 2 models, described by its card as light enough to run on a single consumer GPU. Its card lists vision among the capabilities added since Devstral Small 1.1, so image input is recorded alongside text; the 123B model announced beside it lists no such capability. Its weights are downloadable under an OSI-approved licence, unlike the 123B model, which shows that a shared announcement and a shared family do not imply a shared licence.
intendedUse: Local and on-device software engineering agents.

summary: A mixture-of-experts model published as downloadable weights under an OSI-approved licence, with 119B total and 6.5B activated parameters, a 256k context window, and text and image input with text output. Reasoning is a per-request mode rather than a separate release.
intendedUse: General chat, coding, agentic tasks, and reasoning work, self-deployed or hosted.

summary: A mixture-of-experts model with 1.6T total and 49B activated parameters and a 1M context window, published as downloadable weights under the MIT licence. Its card calls the published weights a preview of the series, which is why the status is preview rather than current. The release date is the day the repository was published on the creator’s verified Hugging Face organization, because no dated announcement on the creator’s own domain could be reached.
intendedUse: Long-context reasoning and agentic work, self-deployed from downloadable weights.

summary: The smaller of the two DeepSeek-V4 models published on the same day, with 284B total and 13B activated parameters and the same 1M context window, under the same MIT licence. The release date is the day the repository was published on the creator’s verified Hugging Face organization, because no dated announcement on the creator’s own domain could be reached.
intendedUse: Long-context work where the Pro model’s size is impractical, self-deployed from downloadable weights.

summary: The generation preceding DeepSeek-V4, published as downloadable weights under the MIT licence and described by its card as introducing DeepSeek Sparse Attention for long-context work. The card states no parameter count and no context window, so neither is recorded rather than being estimated. Its card declares a base model of DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp-Base, which is not itself recorded in this dataset, so no derivation is recorded here either. It precedes DeepSeek-V4 in time, but succession is only recorded between releases of one family, so that ordering is stated here rather than as a relationship record.
intendedUse: Reasoning and agentic work, self-deployed from downloadable weights.

summary: The Opus tier of the Claude 4.6 generation, announced on 5 February 2026. Anthropic describes it as improving on its predecessor for coding, planning, longer agentic tasks, larger codebases, code review, and debugging, and states that it carries a 1M token context window in beta. It is served through the Claude API as claude-opus-4-6 and is listed as Active, with a tentative retirement no sooner than 5 February 2027. Input and output modalities are recorded as text only because the announcement does not state image input for this release.
intendedUse: Coding, agentic work over longer horizons, and everyday knowledge-work tasks such as financial analysis, research, and working with documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.

summary: The Opus tier of the Claude 4.7 generation, announced as generally available on 16 April 2026. Anthropic describes gains in advanced software engineering, long-running task handling, instruction following, and self-verification, and states that the model can see images in greater resolution, which is the basis for recording image input. It is served through the Claude API as claude-opus-4-7 and is listed as Active, with a tentative retirement no sooner than 16 April 2027. No context window is recorded because the announcement does not state one.
intendedUse: Advanced software engineering and complex, long-running agentic tasks, including work involving higher-resolution image input.

summary: The Opus tier of the Claude 4.8 generation, announced on 28 May 2026 as an upgrade to Claude Opus 4.7 and compared to it on tests of coding, agentic skills, reasoning and knowledge work. The model overview page records a 1M token context window, a 128K token maximum output, text and image input to text output, and a status of Active (legacy) with retirement no sooner than 28 May 2027. Anthropic now directs users to Claude Opus 5 for improved performance, which is the basis for recording the status as legacy rather than current. It is served through the Claude API as claude-opus-4-8.
intendedUse: Anthropic compares Claude Opus 4.8 on tests of coding, agentic skills, reasoning and practical knowledge work tasks, and documents it as taking text and image input and producing text output. Anthropic now recommends migrating to Claude Opus 5 for improved performance.

summary: The flagship Qwen3.8 model, a sparse mixture-of-experts system its card states as "2.4T in total and 95B activated" parameters with a native context length of 262,144 tokens, published as downloadable weights under a licence of Alibaba Cloud’s own drafting. The card distinguishes these weights from Qwen3.8-Max, a hosted version with additional features; only the weights are recorded here.
intendedUse: Text generation, coding and long-context work, run from the published weights rather than from a hosted endpoint.

summary: A dense 27B vision-language model in the Qwen3.8 generation, released under Apache-2.0 with a native context length of 262,144 tokens. Its card gives an image-text-to-text pipeline, which is what this record states; Amazon’s hosting announcement also claims video understanding, and the creator’s narrower statement is preferred.
intendedUse: Multimodal understanding over text and images, coding and agentic tasks, either from the published weights or through a platform that hosts them.

featuredRationale: Microsoft AI’s own reasoning model, and the record that shows what a Microsoft-created model looks like next to the Copilot product and the Microsoft Foundry platform.
summary: Microsoft AI’s reasoning model, announced as "a 35B-active, ~1T-total parameters, sparse Mixture of Experts model" supporting "a 256k token window" and available in public preview on Microsoft Foundry. The approximate total parameter count is not recorded, because the announcement gives it only as an approximation and this dataset does not round a hedge into a number.
intendedUse: Reasoning over mathematics, knowledge and agentic coding tasks through a hosted endpoint.

summary: A computer-use agent model from Microsoft Research AI Frontiers that takes a text goal plus screenshots and emits reasoning followed by a tool call, released under the MIT licence with a 262,144-token context length. Its card states it was "supervised fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-27B", a model created by Alibaba Cloud; Microsoft created Fara1.5-27B and Alibaba Cloud created the base it started from, and neither fact makes either the author of the other’s work. Qwen3.5-27B is not recorded in this dataset, so the derivation is stated here rather than linked.
intendedUse: Completing end-to-end web tasks from screenshots, inside the agent harness its card recommends.

summary: Amazon’s speech-to-speech model for real-time conversational AI, which AWS says "unifies speech understanding and generation into a single model" and which adds "cross-modal interaction, allowing users to seamlessly switch between voice and text in the same session" with "a one-million token context window". It is served through Amazon Bedrock, which Amazon also operates; the model and the platform are separate records here even though one company is behind both.
intendedUse: Real-time voice applications built on a bidirectional streaming API, such as conversational assistants and voice-driven support.

summary: Cohere describes it as "a sparse mixture-of-experts model" at "218B total, 25B active" parameters, and as "Cohere's first Mixture of Experts model". It takes text and image input and returns text. Cohere publishes it on two routes at once — its own deployment and an "Open Source Deployment" under an Apache 2.0 licence — which is what the access type records. The licence name is Cohere's own statement; that the licence is OSI-approved is a separate claim resting on OSI's published list, because no Cohere page states it.
intendedUse: Cohere lists it for "Complex, Multimodal Agentic Tasks" and "Multilingual Tasks", reachable either through Cohere's own deployment or self-deployed from downloadable weights.

summary: A fully open 7B base language model from AI2’s second-generation OLMo release, published with open weights, data, and code.
intendedUse: Open research and downstream fine-tuning where reproducible training data and weights are required.

summary: The instruction-tuned 34B member of TII’s Falcon-H1 hybrid attention–state-space series, released with downloadable weights.
intendedUse: Instruction-following and long-context assistant tasks where open weights are needed.

summary: The open-weight 340B base model of NVIDIA’s Nemotron-4 340B release, intended primarily for synthetic data generation.
intendedUse: Generating synthetic training data and serving as a base for further alignment under the NVIDIA Open Model License.

summary: AI21 Labs’ first open-weight hybrid Mamba–Transformer model, a 52B Mixture-of-Experts with 12B active parameters and long context.
intendedUse: Open research and long-context generation; a base release rather than an aligned chat model.

summary: The compact “Air” Mixture-of-Experts model of Zhipu AI’s GLM-4.5 series, with 106B total and 12B active parameters, released with open weights.
intendedUse: Reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks where a smaller open-weight GLM-4.5 model is preferred.

summary: The instruction-tuned member of Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2 series, a 1T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts with 32B active parameters, offered as open weights and via API.
intendedUse: Agentic, tool-use, and coding tasks, available as downloadable weights or through the Moonshot API.

summary: The largest member of EleutherAI’s Pythia suite, trained on the Pile with 154 saved checkpoints per model so that the same training run can be inspected at any step.
intendedUse: Research on the behaviour, functionality, and limitations of large language models; the model card states the suite is not intended for deployment.

license.name: EXAONE AI Model License Agreement 1.1 - NC

summary: The 7.8B instruction-tuned member of LG AI Research’s EXAONE 3.5 series, a bilingual English and Korean model with a 32,768-token context length.
intendedUse: Bilingual English and Korean instruction following and long-context work. The licence is non-commercial, so commercial use is not granted by it.

license.name: EXAONE AI Model License Agreement 1.2 - NC

summary: The 32B member of LG AI Research’s EXAONE 4.0 series, a model integrating a non-reasoning mode and a reasoning mode, supporting English, Korean and Spanish, with a 131,072-token context length. No total parameter count is recorded: the model card's only figure explicitly excludes embeddings, and the page's unqualified figures appear only inside multi-column comparison tables.
intendedUse: Text generation in English, Korean and Spanish, in reasoning or non-reasoning mode, including agentic tool use. Released under the EXAONE AI Model License Agreement 1.2 - NC; the card points commercial use to a separately licensed FriendliAI endpoint.

summary: The instruction-tuned Arctic model from Snowflake AI Research, a dense-MoE hybrid pairing a 10B dense transformer with a 128x3.66B residual MoE MLP for 480B total and 17B active parameters.
intendedUse: Text and code generation from text input, with ungated weights under Apache-2.0. Snowflake’s two pages disagree on the release year; see the source notes.

summary: Upstage’s 22B pre-release of Solar Pro, produced by depth up-scaling a 14B model, with a 4K maximum context length and weights under MIT.
intendedUse: Instruction following on a single GPU. The model card describes this as a pre-release version of the official Solar Pro, so it is recorded with preview status.

summary: IBM’s largest Granite 4.2 model: a 30B dense decoder-only reasoning model post-trained on the Granite 4.1 base, with a thinking / non-thinking switch and weights under Apache 2.0.
intendedUse: IBM describes the generation as built for enterprise and research use, with the 8B and 30B models additionally trained through agentic reinforcement learning for tool calling, code editing and terminal use.

summary: Baidu’s text mixture-of-experts model in the ERNIE 4.5 generation, with 300B total and 47B activated parameters and a 131072-token context length, released under Apache 2.0.
intendedUse: No task or capability claim is recorded beyond the card's Modality: Text row, because the card's only capability language sits in its Modality-Specific Post-Training section — it describes the ERNIE 4.5 LLMs as "optimized for general-purpose language understanding and generation" — and this repository's training stage is left unresolved: the Model Overview prose calls the model Post-trained while the configuration table's Training Stage row reads Pretraining, reconciled nowhere. Recording a post-training capability while the stage is unsettled would assert the contested side, so it is withheld rather than smoothed over. The -PT in the repository name is the card's own label for Transformer-style PyTorch weights rather than a training stage, and the vision-language members of the same generation are not recorded here.

summary: Tencent’s open-weight video foundation model, released with inference code and weights under Tencent’s own community licence, which does not apply in the European Union, United Kingdom or South Korea.
intendedUse: Video generation from text prompts. The card describes the model as having over 13 billion parameters without stating an exact count, so no parameter count is recorded.

summary: ByteDance Seed’s instruction-tuned 36B open-weight model, trained on 12T tokens with a context length the card states as 512K, released under Apache 2.0 alongside its base counterparts.
intendedUse: Instruction following and reasoning. The card states a context length of "512K" rather than an exact token count; the recorded contextWindow applies this dataset’s documented mapping of a stated K figure to a token number.

summary: Stability AI’s 8.1 billion parameter Multimodal Diffusion Transformer, the base model of the Stable Diffusion 3.5 generation, released under the Stability AI Community License.
intendedUse: Text-to-image generation, which Stability describes as suited to professional use at 1 megapixel resolution. The licence is free below a stated annual revenue threshold and requires a separate enterprise agreement above it.

summary: Databricks’ fine-grained mixture-of-experts model with 132B total and 36B active parameters, pre-trained on 12T tokens of text and code, published as downloadable weights and served to Databricks customers through APIs.
intendedUse: General text generation and instruction following. Recorded as both open-weight and hosted because Databricks states the weights are available under an open licence and that DBRX is available to its customers via APIs. The weight repositories were gated at the time of verification.

summary: The 40K thinking-budget version of MiniMax-M1, a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts reasoning model with lightning attention, offered as downloadable weights and through MiniMax’s paid API.
intendedUse: Long-input and extended-reasoning work — the card names complex software engineering, tool use, and long-context tasks — run either from downloaded weights or through the MiniMax API.

summary: The 80K thinking-budget version of MiniMax-M1, a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts reasoning model with lightning attention, offered as downloadable weights and through MiniMax’s paid API.
intendedUse: Long-input and extended-reasoning work — the card names complex software engineering, tool use, and long-context tasks — run either from downloaded weights or through the MiniMax API.

license.name: Apple Machine Learning Research Model License Agreement

summary: The instruction-tuned 3B member of Apple’s OpenELM family, released with downloadable weights under a licence restricting use to scientific research. No context length is stated on any Apple page read for this record, so none is recorded.
intendedUse: Scientific research into efficient language models. The licence shipped with the weights states they are released for the sole purpose of research into artificial intelligence and machine-learning technology, which is why the record carries research status rather than current. The card’s two licence identifiers disagree with each other and the disagreement is recorded on the model card source rather than resolved here.

summary: A 3B parameter model that Hugging Face created rather than hosted, published as fully open weights under Apache 2.0 with dual-mode reasoning. The recorded context window is the 65,536 tokens the card states its shipped configuration is set to; the card separately claims 128k tokens via extrapolation, and both figures are recorded on the model card source.
intendedUse: General text generation and reasoning at the 3B scale. No language fact is recorded for this release because the release schema has no field for natural-language coverage. The card is not in conflict on the point: it names six natively supported languages and three more it trained on with fewer tokens, and its front-matter list carries every one of those but German. That single omission is recorded on the model card source.

summary: The chat-tuned 34B member of 01.AI’s Yi-1.5 series, continuously pre-trained on Yi with a 500B-token corpus and fine-tuned on 3M samples, distributed under Apache 2.0.
intendedUse: General conversation and instruction following. Neither a parameter count nor a context window is recorded: no 01.AI page read states a parameter count in prose, and the card’s context figures are given for the Yi-1.5 family as three alternatives rather than for this variant, so either would be an inference from the model’s name. Both omissions are explained on the model card and repository sources.

summary: MiniMax’s mixture-of-experts language model with 456 billion total parameters and 45.9 billion activated per token, published as downloadable weights under the MiniMax Model License.
intendedUse: General text generation. No context window is recorded: the card states a training context of 1 million tokens and an inference capability of up to 4 million, and neither is an exact token count, so both are recorded on the model card source instead. The MIT licence the card lists applies to the accompanying code and not to these weights.

summary: An experimental general-purpose Japanese language model that Sakana AI produced by merging existing models with its Evolutionary Model Merge method, released as a research prototype. Recorded at month precision because the announcement post’s date, its own retrospective wording, and the repository timestamp do not agree on a day.
intendedUse: Research and development only; the card states the model is an experimental prototype, which is why the record carries research status. The weights ship under Microsoft Research License Terms because a Microsoft model was merged in, which is a licence fact and not an attribution: the card names Sakana AI as the developer and this dataset records Sakana AI as the creator. The three merged input models are not recorded entities here, so no derivation links are recorded.

summary: Sarvam AI’s multilingual hybrid-reasoning language model, post-trained from Mistral Small on Indian languages alongside English and published under Apache 2.0.
intendedUse: Multilingual text generation and reasoning across Indian languages and English. No context window is recorded, because no Sarvam AI page read for this record states one. The recorded parameter figure is the 24B label Sarvam AI applies to this model in its announcement post's comparison tables, which the Hub's measurement of this model's own weights at 23.57 billion rounds to. The base model is not a recorded release here, so the derivation is stated in prose rather than as a link.

license.name: HyperCLOVA X SEED Model License Agreement

summary: An instruction-tuned text model, one of the three lightweight HyperCLOVA X SEED models NAVER announced as its first major generative AI release made free and open source for commercial use. No context window is recorded: every statement of the length is a bare “16k” and the Hugging Face repository is access-gated, so its config.json could not be read and no exact figure exists in any source here. The version is recorded as 1 because the model’s own name carries none and no source states one.
intendedUse: General text understanding and generation, with the card reporting competitive results on Korean-language and Korean-culture benchmarks. NAVER’s announcement states these weights may be downloaded and used commercially or academically free of charge.

summary: A 7B foundation model announced by Aleph Alpha as publicly available under the Open Aleph License, engineered for concise, length-controlled responses and culturally and linguistically optimized for German, French and Spanish. The licence permits non-commercial research and educational use only, so the model is recorded as open-weight with osiApproved false. The version is recorded as 1 because the family name carries no other and the model's name states none.
intendedUse: Length-controlled text generation for domain-specific applications, which the announcement highlights particularly in the automotive and engineering industries. Aleph Alpha states the weights are publicly available under the Open Aleph License for non-commercial research and educational use.

summary: A 21-billion-parameter open-source reasoning model that Reka describes as an update to Reka Flash 3, post-trained with supervised finetuning followed by large-scale reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. Reka reports it improves by 10 points on LiveCodeBench v5 over Reka Flash 3 and is competitive with models such as Qwen3-32B on coding tasks.
intendedUse: Coding and reasoning tasks, and use as a base model to be finetuned on agentic tasks, per Reka's own statement. Reka open-sources the weights on Hugging Face and also serves the model via its API.

summary: A 14B hybrid-mode reasoning model based on Qwen 3 14B, described on its card as "a frontier, hybrid-mode reasoning model based on Qwen 3 14B by Nous Research that is aligned to you". Its licence slug (apache-2.0) and its declared base (Qwen/Qwen3-14B, itself Apache-2.0) agree, so the Apache-2.0 record rests on two mutually-consistent statements. Nous lists it as "Small and dense Hermes variant for local inference" on its releases page.
intendedUse: Steerable general reasoning and assistant tasks with an optional explicit thinking mode, aimed at local inference per Nous Research's own release listing.

summary: A 1.2-billion-parameter on-device foundation model, the largest of three dense LFM2 checkpoints Liquid released. Its own blog states LFM2 is built on a hybrid architecture of "16 blocks: 10 double-gated short-range convolution blocks and 6 blocks of grouped query attention", so despite the Liquid branding it is a hybrid attention model rather than a pure non-transformer, and it is recorded as language-reasoning without any non-transformer claim.
intendedUse: Fast on-device and edge text generation on CPU, GPU and NPU hardware, per Liquid's own positioning of LFM2 for local and edge use cases.

summary: A 7B reinforcement-learning reasoning checkpoint from Xiaomi's MiMo-7B series. It is the specific snapshot the repository's only dated update line names: "[2025.05.30] We scaled the SFT dataset from approximately 500K to 6M instances and continuously expanding the RL training window size from 32K to 48K, the performance of MiMo-7B-RL-0530 ... can be continuously improved". The earlier MiMo-7B-RL checkpoint carries no dated line, so this 0530 snapshot is recorded rather than it.
intendedUse: Mathematical and code reasoning, where Xiaomi reports the 0530 checkpoint reaches 80.1 on AIME 2024 and 60.9 on LiveCodeBench v5.

summary: AI Singapore's 8B SEA-LION v3 model, a continued pre-training of Llama 3.1 8B for Southeast-Asian languages. Its family documentation records "Llama-SEA-LION-v3-8B, based on Llama 3.1 8B, now provides a larger context length of 128K", which the recorded context window rests on. The release is dated at month precision because the only date any source states for SEA-LION v3 is "released in Dec 2024"; no day is recorded rather than inventing one.
intendedUse: Natural-language reasoning and instruction following in Southeast-Asian languages, per AI Singapore's statement that SEA-LION v3 offers "enhanced natural language reasoning (NLR) abilities and superior instruction-following in SEA languages".

summary: The chat-tuned 34B member of 01.AI’s original Yi series, opened to the public on 2023-11-23 alongside the rest of the chat models. Its card declares Apache 2.0; the repository README records a Yi Series Models Community License Agreement update on the same date, and both statements are kept on the sources rather than reconciled.
intendedUse: General conversation and instruction following. Neither a parameter count nor a context window is recorded: no 01.AI page read states either in prose for this variant, so a figure would have to be inferred from the model’s name, and the same omission is already made for Yi-1.5-34B-Chat.

summary: The first Qwen3.5 release, a sparse mixture-of-experts model its card states as “397B in total and 17B activated” parameters with a native context length of 262,144 tokens, published as downloadable weights under Apache-2.0. The card describes it as a causal language model with a vision encoder and also carries a video-input quickstart example; the narrower vision-language statement is what this record states. Qwen3.5-Plus, described on the same card as the hosted version corresponding to these weights, is a separate artefact and is not recorded here.
intendedUse: Multimodal understanding over text and images, coding and agentic work, either from the published weights or through a platform that hosts them.

summary: The first open-weight Qwen3.6 variant, a sparse mixture-of-experts model its card states as “35B in total and 3B activated” parameters with a native context length of 262,144 tokens, published under Apache-2.0. Its card presents the generation as following the February 2026 Qwen3.5 series and emphasises agentic coding. As with the Qwen3.5 card, the declared type is a causal language model with a vision encoder while a video-input quickstart also appears; the narrower statement is recorded.
intendedUse: Agentic and repository-level coding work and multimodal understanding over text and images, from the published weights or a platform that hosts them.
